info.name: Kit Taxi Driver API
info.description:
Kit Taxi Driver API — the driver onboarding backend. Node.js, Express, TypeScript, MySQL.

Every request carries the response a real run returned, saved as an example, so the shape is readable without a server.

Only the successful call is kept here. Every refusal the API can answer with — the 401s, 422s and 409s, with the code and fields each one sends — is in Kit-Taxi-Driver-API.openapi.json beside this file, which is the better place to look one up.

TO RUN IT LIVE
Start the API with `npm run dev`, then select the "Kit Taxi Driver · Dev" environment. The Prod environment ships with an empty baseUrl — fill it in once the API is deployed.

AUTH
Two kinds of token, and neither opens the other's endpoints.

Nothing has to be copied by hand. A script on the collection reads every response and sets authToken, refreshToken, driverId and adminToken as it goes, so running the folders in order just works.

A driver's: the sign-in calls are public, and GET /session straight after /verifyOTP takes the verified number rather than a token. Every protected call after it sends the authToken as a bearer token.

An admin's: POST /admin/login fills adminToken, which the /admin calls send. On an empty database the first POST /admin/signup is activated as Super Admin; every account after it waits for one of those to approve it, so it cannot sign in yet.

RESPONSE SHAPE
Every endpoint answers { success: true, data } or { success: false, error }. error.code is stable and the only thing to switch on; error.message says what went wrong in plain words; error.fields names the rejected inputs. Every key is camelCase.

SWAGGER
Kit-Taxi-Driver-API.openapi.json, generated beside this file, holds the full schema. Import that into Swagger rather than converting this collection.

item.name: 01 · App launch
item.description: Read once on launch: branding, the country list, and the documents to collect.

request.description:
Everything the app needs before its first screen paints, and the only call it can make without a token.

Serves the sign-in screen end to end:
• branding — wordmark, logo, the map behind the welcome copy, and the headline text, so wording changes need no app release
• theme — colours, corner radii and typefaces as tokens rather than values hard-coded in the app
• auth.methods — drives the Phone / Email toggle. One entry means the app shows no toggle
• auth.countries — the GB +44 picker, with preselected saying which one it opens on
• auth.social — Apple and Google. A disabled provider is omitted rather than returned as enabled:false, so the app renders what it is given and decides nothing
• legal — the two footer links, each with a version that is sent back on acceptance so consent is auditable

Cacheable for five minutes; it changes on deploy, not per request.

item.name: 03 · Sign up
item.description: The "Become a driver" form. Nothing is written until the code is proved.

request.description:
Checks the details and sends a code, and returns nothing but success. Nothing is written to a driver yet: the details ride on the code, so a form nobody finishes leaves no account behind, and nobody can rewrite an account they have not proved they own.

gender is optional, one of MALE, FEMALE or OTHER, and is stored as the driver's word rather than a checked fact: it shows on their profile and cannot switch gender-specific riding on. Approving their application confirms it, because that is when somebody has read the identity document — see 14 · Ride preferences.

item.name: 05 · Session
item.description: Everything the app knows about the signed-in driver, on every launch.

request.description:
The first call after /verifyOTP. The driver holds no token yet, so the number they just verified says who they are. Encode the + as %2B.

Returns the tokens, who the driver is, what they may do, and every document grouped the way the screens are. The proof it spends is one-use and lasts two minutes.

item.name: 06 · Refresh the session
item.description: A new pair of tokens, so an expiry is never a sign-in screen.

item.name: Get a new pair of tokens

request.description:
The auth token is short-lived, so the app calls this quietly in the background rather than sending the driver back to the sign-in screen every hour. expiresIn on the session response says when to.

The proof travels in the body, not the Authorization header — by the time this is called the auth token has usually expired, so it cannot be renewed with itself. Sending an auth token here answers WRONG_TOKEN_TYPE.

Both tokens come back replaced, so a phone in regular use never reaches the refresh token's own expiry and never asks the driver to sign in again for no reason.

item.name: 07 · Upload documents
item.description: Every upload, on every screen, through one call keyed by document id.

request.description:
Every identity document in one call. The body is keyed by document name, so send as many or as few as you have — one tile on its own works the same way, and sending one never clears another.

type is the dropdown choice, checked against the choices in the session response — the tiles a card asks for follow it, so a passport wants two and a birth certificate one. images is keyed by slot name. fields carries the typed boxes that sit beside the photos.

expiry is YYYY-MM; the screen shows it as 08 / 2031. An expiry in the past is refused here rather than being found days later during review.

With every slot filled and both boxes in, canContinue turns true.

item.name: 11 · Rides
item.description: Finished work: the history list and one ride in full.

request.description:
The history screen. Rides come back newest first, already grouped into local days with a count and a total per day — which day a ride belongs to is a timezone question, and the client would need the same zone and arithmetic to make its own totals agree.

Paging is on a cursor, not an offset: send loadMoreBefore straight back as ?loadMoreBefore= and nothing is skipped or repeated if a ride is written mid-scroll. Null means there is nothing older, which is what hides "Load earlier rides".

thisWeek counts the week however far the list has been scrolled and whichever status is being looked at, because that is what the header shows.

?status=completed|cancelled is what the filter control narrows the list to. A cancelled Nothing in a ride is null. A cancellation still carries its destinationAddress and endTime, and its distanceInKm and durationInMinutes are zero rather than absent — nothing was driven. The app picks what to show by status, not by checking for nulls.

item.name: 12 · Earnings
item.description: What the driver made, by day and by period.

request.description:
The earnings screen. period is today, week or month, matching its three tabs, and defaults to week.

dailyEarnings holds one bar per day in the period, zeroes included — a gap would read as missing data rather than a day off. The peak the chart marks is simply the largest of them.

percentageChangeFromLastPeriod compares with the period before this one, and is null when that period earned nothing, because the change is then not a number anything can render.

onlineTimeInMinutes is time available for work, not time on a trip: the gap between two jobs counts. It comes from driver_shifts, clipped to the period, so a shift spanning midnight counts towards both days.

Weeks run Monday to Sunday and months are calendar months, both worked out in the configured timezone rather than UTC.

item.name: 14 · Ride preferences
item.description: Gender-specific riding: what the driver asked for, and whether it is being honoured.

request.description:
Three things decide whether this driver is matched by passenger gender, and all three have to agree: the feature is switched on for everyone, the driver has a gender recorded, and they have turned the mode on themselves.

isGenderSpecificModeOn is the answer to that whole question, not the stored toggle. Switching features.genderPreference off reads false here for every driver, while each driver's own choice stays stored and comes back by itself when the feature returns — nobody is asked to set it again.

driverGender is what the driver gave at sign-up, or what an admin set. Null is the one thing that stops the toggle, and is what the screen explains.

canTurnOnGenderSpecificMode is whether this driver may use the feature at all. The app could work it out from the fields above and should not have to — eligibility is the server's answer to give, so the rule behind it can gain a condition without an app release. A false here is what a PATCH turning the mode on would refuse.

The labels and the paragraph explaining the feature belong to the app, as everywhere else. Only this driver's state travels.

item.name: 17 · Send status
item.description: Deciding an application — accepted, or rejected with the documents to redo.

request.description:
What an admin sends when an application is nearly right. It reopens the uploads and writes the note the driver reads on their status screen.

documents is keyed the same way a PATCH /documents body is: id is the document id from GET /session. image narrows it to one photograph — front, back, left or right — and may be left out to send the whole document back. reason is required on every entry, because without it the driver gets a card telling them nothing.

The admin's name is taken from the token, never the body.

THE OTHER DECISIONS ON THIS ENDPOINT
Accept it:            { "action": "approve_application" }
Refuse it outright:   { "action": "reject_application", "reason": "…" }

approve_application needs nothing else — an approval has no note and no documents to name. Both it and reject_application are terminal: the transition table allows nothing after either, so a second decision is refused as INVALID_TRANSITION. request_changes is the only one that reopens the uploads and puts a note on the driver's status screen.
